verdicts.title: BLT parameter table publishes a non-existent `error` knob and a `max_buffers` range whose upper half is hard-rejected
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every link. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:195 still publishes a row `| `error` | `"max"` or `"mean"` | Error metric to optimize. `"max"` is conservative. |` and :206-208 a Tips bullet advising how to choose between the two values. `inspect.signature(blt_strategy)` under `uv run` is `(*, max_buffers: 'int' = 10, momentum: 'float' = 1.0, lr_schedule: 'Schedule | None' = None)` - no `error`; the value is hard-coded `error="max"` at packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_blt.py:83 inside `_blt_optimize_cached`, and the trainer's allow-list for the same strategy is `frozenset({"max_buffers", "momentum", "lr_schedule"})` at packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:231, so `error` is nowhere on the public surface. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:196 publishes `max_buffers | 1 - 20 (default 10)`, while packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_blt_math.py:45 sets `_MAX_OPTIMIZATION_BUFFERS = 15` and :1290-1293 raises ConfigurationError above it. Executed: `blt_strategy(max_buffers=16)` constructs fine, then `mf_gaussian(1.0, s, n_steps=500, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5)` -> `ConfigurationError: max_buffers > 15 will likely cause numerical issues.`; the same call with max_buffers=15 returns 21.457. The table also omits `momentum` and `lr_schedule` (lr_schedule is discussed in prose at blt.md:87; momentum is not named on the page at all). Searched for a way out and found none: no deprecated alias, no kwargs passthrough, no config gate. Not tracked: open umbrella #775 ('Reconcile documentation and citations with post-remediation code') declares that implementation lives in sub-issues, its reference-table sweep child is closed, and its only open child #845 is the citation sweep - so this residue of the closed OPQ-358 is not covered by an open issue. Severity lowered from medium to low: docs-only, no epsilon or numerical impact, and the out-of-range case fails loudly at the first epsilon query with a self-explanatory message rather than silently.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md's BLT parameter guide (lines 190-208) disagrees with the code in three ways. (1) It documents an `error` parameter with `"max"`/`"mean"` values plus a Tips bullet on choosing between them, but `blt_strategy` has no such parameter and the trainer's `mf_blt` key allow-list rejects it; the value is hard-coded to `"max"` at _blt.py:83, so the documented 'mean' behaviour is unreachable. (2) It publishes the range `max_buffers | 1 - 20`, while any value above 15 is rejected: `blt_strategy(max_buffers=16)` builds, and the first accounting query (`mf_gaussian(1.0, s, n_steps=500, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5)`) raises `ConfigurationError: max_buffers > 15 will likely cause numerical issues.` (max_buffers=15 succeeds, returning epsilon 21.457). (3) The table omits the two parameters `blt_strategy` actually accepts besides max_buffers - `momentum` and `lr_schedule`. Loud failure, no privacy impact; cost is a misled reader and a wasted debugging cycle for anyone picking 16-20 from the published range.

verdicts.title: README and installation-guide extras block drops the JetBrains index and installs an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`; six of the ten sub-distribution names are unclaimed on PyPI
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. README.md:64-81 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:18-37 pin `--index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` on the primary `pip install opaque` / `uv add opaque` commands and then, in the 'Extras' block directly below, issue four bare commands with no index: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. AGENTS.md:126-138 ('Installation matrix') is index-less for all eleven of its commands. PyPI facts verified by direct API calls: `opaque` is 200 at version 1.0.0, author 'Stefan Marsiske', home_page https://github.com/stef/libopaque, summary 'python libopaque wrapper'; its only artifact is an sdist whose `top_level.txt` is `opaque` and which ships a regular `opaque/__init__.py`. Names 404 (unregistered, open to takeover): opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers, opaque-alignment. Names 200 as defensive stubs at 999.9.9 uploaded 2026-08-12: opaque-dpftrl, opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing, opaque-optimizers. So exactly six of the ten sub-distributions are unprotected, as claimed. The JetBrains index does serve the real names (spot-checked opaque, opaque-base, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-transformers -> all 200), so the pinned command is sound and the defect is precisely the missing pin in the extras blocks. Actually executed the documented command in a clean venv with pip 26.2.1: `pip install --dry-run "opaque[all]"` -> `Collecting opaque[all] / Using cached opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz / WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all' / Would install opaque-1.0.0 pysodium-0.7.18`. pip warns and proceeds, exactly as claimed - no modern-pip hard error rescues the user. Not in milestones-open.tsv or other-open-issues.tsv. One sub-claim I discounted rather than accepted: the finding's 'worse' variant (the foreign distribution replacing an already-installed namespace root) is overstated - in a single venv every opaque-* wheel unpacks into the same site-packages/opaque/ directory, so libopaque's `__init__.py` converting it to a regular package does not by itself hide sibling subpackages; I removed that from the scenario. Severity kept at medium: no privacy or correctness impact on a working install, but the documented command reproducibly installs a foreign package, and six distribution names are genuinely squattable by anyone.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reads README.md (or docs/getting-started/installation.md) top to bottom and copies a command from the 'Extras' block, which - unlike the block immediately above it - carries no `--index-url`. Verified in a clean venv with pip 26.2.1: `pip install "opaque[all]"` resolves against PyPI, prints `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'`, and installs `opaque 1.0.0` (Stefan Marsiske's libopaque ctypes wrapper, which owns the top-level `opaque` package) plus pysodium - not Opaque. The user's subsequent `import opaque.dpsgd...` fails with no hint that the wrong distribution was fetched. Separately, AGENTS.md's index-less installation matrix names six distributions that are unregistered on PyPI (opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers, opaque-alignment), where the four other sub-names already carry 999.9.9 dependency-confusion stubs; anyone can claim the six and serve arbitrary code to a reader following that matrix or to any resolver that falls back to PyPI.

verdicts.title: The RNG-key guide's reproducibility snippet raises InputTypeError
verdicts.reasoning: Copied docs/user-guide/rng-key.md:274-288 verbatim into a file and ran it under `uv run`. It fails at the 8th line of the block: `noisy1, _ = noise_fn(grads, s1)` -> packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:302 -> :322 `opaque.api.base.exceptions.InputTypeError: gaussian_noise expects ClippedPytree inputs. Wrap manual values with opaque.types.clipped(...).` The cause is rng-key.md:279 `grads = {"w": torch.randn(100)}` - a bare dict. Checked the rest of the docs tree for the same pattern: `grep -rn 'noise_fn(' docs/` returns ~30 sites, and every other one binds `grads` from a `grad_fn` / `compute_dp_grads` call inside non-runnable pseudo-code (docs/reference/rng.md:324 included, i.e. the OPQ-362 sibling page is fine), so rng-key.md:282/285 is the only executable-verbatim instance. Nothing in CI executes docs snippets - open umbrella #775 itself notes 'closed #416 left no executable-docs check in CI' - so this cannot be caught automatically. Severity stays low: docs-only, fails immediately with an error message that states the fix.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The 'Reproducibility' snippet at docs/user-guide/rng-key.md:274-288 - the one self-contained runnable block on the page - passes a bare `{"w": torch.randn(100)}` to `noise_fn`. Run verbatim it aborts at `noisy1, _ = noise_fn(grads, s1)` with `InputTypeError: gaussian_noise expects ClippedPytree inputs. Wrap manual values with opaque.types.clipped(...)` (_gaussian.py:322), so the page never demonstrates its own claim that identical keys reproduce identical noise. Fix is one line: `grads = clipped({"w": torch.randn(100)}, max_norm=1.0)` from `opaque.types`. No privacy or numerical impact; no CI check executes docs snippets, so it will not self-correct.

verdicts.title: Published tutorial output embeds a maintainer's absolute local path, username and internal branch name on the public documentation site
verdicts.reasoning: Verified in the tree and on the live site. `grep -rn 'Users/' docs/tutorials/*.ipynb` hits only docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb lines 153, 455, 464, each a stored warning-stream output containing `/Users/evgeny.grigorenko/Workspaces/copilot-worktrees/opaque/evgri243-issue-416-execute-documentation-examples-and-valid-38f84f/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/...` (peft/tuners/lora/layer.py:2285, transformers/integrations/sdpa_attention.py:92, torch/autograd/graph.py:865); no `/home/<user>` paths anywhere in docs/tutorials. mkdocs.yml:59-61 sets `mkdocs-jupyter: include_source: true, execute: false`, and mkdocs.yml:140 puts the notebook in the published nav, so committed outputs are what ships. .github/workflows/docs.yml deploys via mike/GitHub Pages on every push to main, and no nbstripout / ClearOutputPreprocessor step exists anywhere in mkdocs.yml, the workflows, or pre-commit. Closed the chain against the live site rather than stopping at the inference: `curl -L https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/latest/tutorials/llm_finetuning/` returns HTTP 200 and contains the string `evgeny.grigorenko` three times, with the full worktree path and issue-416 branch name intact. Not in either open-issue list. Severity stays low: it is release hygiene - a username, a local workspace layout, the agent-worktree convention and an internal branch name - with no functional, numerical or privacy consequence.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb stores three warning outputs containing `/Users/evgeny.grigorenko/Workspaces/copilot-worktrees/opaque/evgri243-issue-416-execute-documentation-examples-and-valid-38f84f/.venv/...` (nb JSON lines 153, 455, 464). Because mkdocs.yml sets `execute: false` and the notebook is in the published nav, these strings are served verbatim: the live page https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/latest/tutorials/llm_finetuning/ (HTTP 200, fetched) contains the full path three times. Any visitor to the 'Fine-tuning an LLM' tutorial reads a maintainer's OS username, local workspace layout, the copilot-worktrees convention and an internal issue-416 branch name. Nothing breaks; the exposure is durable because no CI step strips or normalizes notebook outputs.
